svg.text: Sweeping the skew bound — where "late" comes from
0s→15/2 late · 60s→15/1 late · 120s→15/1 late · 180s→19/0 late · correct at 141s
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being summed · key = which SOURCE it came from
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in PROCESSING order (tools/stream_seed.js).
7 // EVENTS[7] = (id 7, key "b", et 50, pt 280, v 4) <- the straggler
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the window width, in seconds of event time. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: LAG — the assumed worst-case skew, in seconds. LAG = 60
11 // primitive: W0 — the window this chapter follows. W0 = 0 ([12:00, 12:02))
12 // primitive: KEYS — the source names. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
13 // primitive: max(xs) — the largest element. max([1, 3, 2]) = 3
14 // primitive: min(xs) — the smallest element. min([1, 3, 2]) = 1
15 // primitive: winOf(et) — the START of the WIN-second window holding et.
17 // primitive: sum(ids) — total v over those event ids.
19 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
21 type Verdict { lag, closedAt, published, lateIds }
23 // primitive: LAG_MIN — the smallest skew bound that makes W0 correct. LAG_MIN = 141
24 // derived: max event time seen BEFORE the straggler (260) − the window end (120) + 1
25 // primitive: maxEtThrough(i) — the highest event time in EVENTS[0 .. i].
28 // function: watermarkAt(i, lag) — the heuristic, parameterised by the bound.
34 // function: closesAt(winStart, lag) — the first index at which that window fires.
38 if (watermarkAt(i, lag) >= winStart + WIN) { return i }
43 // function: isLate(e, i, lag) — was this event's window already closed when it
44 // arrived? Note it asks about the WINDOW, never about the event's own skew.
52 // function: evaluate(lag) — one skew bound, judged on W0 and on lateness.
59 if (winOf(EVENTS[i].et) == W0 && i <= c) { ids = append(ids, EVENTS[i].id) }
60 if (isLate(EVENTS[i], i, lag)) { bad = append(bad, EVENTS[i].id) }
65 // function: main() — THE CALLER: the same stream, four skew bounds.
Step 3/0 — one second below the threshold is still wrong
`evaluate(140)` publishes 15, the same as the default. The watermark reaches 120 before the straggler arrives, which is still ≥ 120, so W0 has closed. The
threshold is not approximate — it is a single comparison flipping.
